results.name: gfw_fishing_effort_daily_most_recent
results.title: Global Fishing Watch - Daily Fishing Intensity (Most Recent)
results.description:
Overview

This feature service provides a global view of the most recent daily fishing intensity records published by Global Fishing Watch. It supports near-current monitoring of fishing effort using rolling recent data that accounts for reporting latency and preserves a short historical window for continuity in summaries and analysis.

Layer

  • Global Fishing Watch - Daily Fishing Intensity (Most Recent): A global feature layer of daily fishing effort observations, including fishing hours, gear type, vessel counts, location, and record age. The layer supports visualization and analysis of the latest fishing activity patterns.

Geographic Coverage

The service covers global waters and is suitable for worldwide fishing activity monitoring and spatial comparison.

Use Cases

  • Monitoring recent fishing activity patterns
  • Supporting fisheries intelligence and situational awareness
  • Summarizing fishing effort by day, gear type, and area
  • Visualizing vessel activity in web maps and dashboards

More information can be found here: https://globalfishingwatch.org/our-apis/documentation 

Below is a list of the various gear types for fishing that are found in the layer.  Some gear types require slower travel and therefor occupy a particular space for longer durations of time.

results.name: SAR_Fixed_Infrastructure
results.title: Global SAR Fixed Infrastructure Datasets API
results.description:
Offshore fixed infrastructure is a global dataset that is accessible through the Global Fishing Watch Datasets API. It uses AI and machine learning to detect and classify structures throughout the world’s oceans. This is the same API used in our Public Map, which means that we are filtering the data compared to the Data Download Portal. In the Map and API, we exclude data labeled as noise, lake_maracaibo is relabeled oil, only structures that have been detected for at least 3 months and have a predicted noise probability of < .3 are included, and data from certain regions, such as Chile, Canada, and Norway are filtered to remove additional noisy detections. Specifically, we are removing these coordinates:

  • (lat BETWEEN -50.6 AND -41.51 AND lon BETWEEN -80.44 AND -75.71) -- Chile
  • (lat BETWEEN 50.6 AND 74.02 AND lon BETWEEN -115.8 AND -60.53) -- Canada
  • (lat BETWEEN 64.2 AND 67.43 AND lon BETWEEN 10.58 AND 16.06) -- Norway_s
  • (lat BETWEEN 67.63 AND 71.19 AND lon BETWEEN 12.44 AND 31.08) -- Norway_n

Classification labels (oil, wind, and unknown) are provided, as well as confidence levels (high, medium, or low) reflecting our certainty in the assigned label. Detections can be filtered and colored on the map using both label and confidence level. The data is updated monthly, and new classified detections are added at the beginning of every month. Viewing change over time allows anyone to recognize the rapid industrialization of the world’s oceans. For example, you can easily observe the expansion of wind farms in the North and East China Seas, or changes in oil infrastructure in the Gulf of Mexico or the Persian Gulf. 

The availability of Global Fishing Watch data in ArcGIS Online allows users to explore key maritime patterns more seamlessly within their existing GIS workflows. From analyzing synthetic aperture radar (SAR) vessel detections near offshore infrastructure to monitoring vessel presence or fishing intensity within sensitive areas, these layers support a wide range of ocean research, enforcement, and planning needs. The offshore fixed infrastructure dataset is a first-of-its-kind public resource that sheds light on the industrialization of our seas and enables new approaches to marine spatial analysis and decision-making across sectors.

For more information, please see the SAR (Synthetic-Aperture Radar) Data Caveats and Terms of Use in the Global Fishing Watch API documentation for details on Global Fishing Watch data, API licenses, and rate limits.

The Global Fishing Watch layers are accessible through this ArcGIS Online Group: https://globalfishingw.maps.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=c5319e7d98cd4941b11d2ebdb85641b3

results.name: fishing_effort_hours_yearly_v02
results.title: Global AIS Apparent Fishing Effort (Yearly) 4Wings API
results.description:
The AIS Apparent Fishing Effort is part of the 4Wings API (aka Map Visualization), which provides fast visualization, navigation, and analysis of gridded spatiotemporal datasets. The API provides access to three core datasets that enable comprehensive analysis of maritime activity. To determine “apparent fishing effort,” Global Fishing Watch analyzes automatic identification system (AIS) data collected from vessels that our research has identified as known or possible commercial fishing vessels and applies a fishing detection algorithm based on changes in vessel speed and direction. The algorithm classifies each AIS broadcast data point for these vessels as either apparently fishing or not fishing and shows the activity on the Global Fishing Watch apparent fishing effort heat map. To learn more, read the Global Fishing Watch AIS-based fishing activity methodology paper.

Global Fishing Watch uses data about a vessel’s identity, type, location, speed, direction and more that is broadcast using the Automatic Identification System (AIS) and collected via satellites and terrestrial receivers. AIS was developed for safety/collision-avoidance. AIS data as broadcast may vary in completeness, accuracy and quality. Also, data collection by satellite or terrestrial receivers may introduce errors through missing or inaccurate data. Global Fishing Watch’s fishing presence algorithm is a best effort to mathematically identify “apparent fishing activity.” As a result, some fishing activity may not be identified as such by Global Fishing Watch; conversely, Global Fishing Watch may show apparent fishing activity where fishing is not actually taking place. For these reasons, Global Fishing Watch qualifies designations of vessel fishing activity, including synonyms of the term “fishing activity,” such as “fishing” or “fishing effort,” as “apparent,” rather than certain. Any/all Global Fishing Watch information about “apparent fishing activity” should be considered an estimate and must be relied upon solely at your own risk.

For more information, please see the Data Caveats and Terms of Use in the Global Fishing Watch API documentation for details on GFW data, API licenses, and rate limits.
results.snippet: The AIS Apparent Fishing Effort shows the estimated number of hours of apparent fishing activity per square kilometer per year, based on AIS data. It is derived from vessels equipped with AIS transponders and analyzed using a machine learning algorithm that identifies patterns consistent with fishing behavior. This layer is aggregated from the AIS Fishing Effort (Daily). Data is from 2012 until ~72 hours ago.

results.name: sar_detection_yearly_unmatched_v02
results.title: Global SAR Vessel Detections - Unmatched (Yearly) 4Wings API
results.description:
Global Fishing Watch uses Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) to detect at-sea vessels and structures in any weather conditions. Spaceborne SAR is a satellite-based sensor that shoots microwaves to the Earth's surface and measures the amplitude and phase of the signals that are reflected back from objects on the ground and water, known as backscatter. We use SAR imagery from the Copernicus Sentinel-1 mission of the European Space Agency, sourced from polar-orbiting satellites (S1A and, formerly, S1B), to detect all vessels in each scene. Our detection approach combines a modified version of a standard constant false alarm rate (CFAR) method with modern machine learning to identify vessels in SAR imagery and filter out false positives. Detections that cannot be reliably matched with AIS transmissions are included in this layer. Those that are matched are excluded and instead available in the Global SAR Vessel Detections – Matched layer. For more information, check the Paper Paolo et al. 2024, Nature.

This detection approach consists of identifying pixels with a “brightness” level above the mean background backscatter, representing the sea clutter around the target, and then using machine learning to filter and improve the results. For unmatched detections, Global Fishing Watch applies an experimental machine-learning model to estimate whether the detected behavior is likely to be fishing or non-fishing. This estimation considers vessel size, location, proximity to port, and environmental factors to estimate the likelihood that the detection is associated with a fishing vessel. 

For more information, please see the Data Caveats and Terms of Use in the Global Fishing Watch API documentation for details on Global Fishing Watch data, API licenses, and rate limits.

results.name: sar_detection_monthly_matched_v02
results.title: Global SAR Vessel Detections - Matched (Monthly) 4Wings API
results.description:
Global Fishing Watch uses Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) to detect at-sea vessels and structures in any weather conditions. Spaceborne SAR is a satellite-based sensor that shoots microwaves to the Earth's surface and measures the amplitude and phase of the signals that are reflected back from objects on the ground and water, known as backscatter. We use SAR imagery from the Copernicus Sentinel-1 mission of the European Space Agency, sourced from polar-orbiting satellites (S1A and, formerly, S1B), to detect all vessels in each scene. Our approach combines a modified version of a well-established ship detection method (constant false alarm rate) with modern machine learning to estimate detection sizes and eliminate false detections. This detection approach consists of identifying pixels with a “brightness” level above the mean background backscatter, representing the sea clutter around the target, and then using machine learning to filter and improve the results. For more information, check the Paper Paolo et al. 2024, Nature.

For detections that are successfully matched with a likely AIS observation, we include them in this layer. Detections that cannot be matched are excluded here but are available in the Global SAR Vessel Detections – Unmatched layer. For unmatched detections, we apply an experimental machine learning model to estimate whether the behavior is likely to be fishing or non-fishing, based on factors such as vessel length, location, distance from port, and environmental conditions. For more information, please see the Data Caveats and Terms of Use in the Global Fishing Watch API documentation for details on Global Fishing Watch data, API licenses, and rate limits.

results.name: vessel_presence_hours_daily_v02
results.title: Global AIS Vessel Presence (Daily) 4Wings API
results.description:
AIS Vessel Presence (Daily) is part of the 4Wings API (also known as Map Visualization), which allows for fast visualization, navigation, and analysis of gridded spatiotemporal datasets. The API provides access to three core datasets that enable comprehensive maritime activity analysis. 

Global Fishing Watch uses data about a vessel’s identity, type, location, speed, direction and more that is broadcast using the Automatic Identification System (AIS) and collected via satellites and terrestrial receivers. AIS was developed for safety/collision-avoidance. The activity layer displays a heatmap of vessel presence. The presence is determined by taking one position per hour per vessel from the positions transmitted by the vessel's AIS. The vessel presence layer, analyzes AIS data collected from vessels identified by our research. Unlike the apparent fishing effort layers, the presence layer is not limited to fishing vessels. The presence is determined from positions transmitted by the vessel’s AIS and displayed as a heatmap.

For more information, please see the Data Caveats and Terms of Use in the Global Fishing Watch API documentation for details on Global Fishing Watch data, API licenses, and rate limits.
